note: 12 claims: 8 confirmed, 4 corrected, 0 unverified; the new guide now gets the token endpoint, Basic auth, 1-day tokens, refresh and api_base_url_for_customer right, but it drops the permanent shared/personal authorization setting and the exact Admin center path, and still omits api:users:read for its GET /v2/users test.

rows.composio: Any user with Admin Centre access.
rows.ours: A Gong tech admin creates and authorizes the app; notes the create page says any Gong plan.
rows.provider: "Who can use this: Tech admin. Available on: Any Gong plan."

rows.claim: A Gong developer instance is needed first
rows.ours: Request a developer instance via Gong's form; up to five working days (wait modelled 0-7 days).
rows.provider: "Step 1: Request a developer instance... This can take up to five working days."

rows.composio: Admin Centre → Ecosystem → API → Integrations tab → Create Integration.
rows.ours: "Open Admin center and add the integration"; an open question says to find the page where you create the app.
rows.provider: Admin center → Settings tab → API (Ecosystem card) → Integrations tab → CREATE INTEGRATION (partners see the link as API/MCP Server).

rows.claim: Authorization context is permanent and personal access is limited
rows.ours: Not covered (only says a tech admin must authorize).
rows.provider: Shared vs personal access is chosen at submission and "can't be edited once the integration is set up"; personal access supports only api:ai-ask:read, api:ai-briefer:read and all mcp scopes; shared access must be connected by a tech admin.

rows.composio: Must match exactly, no trailing slash.
rows.ours: Redirect URI must match one registered with the integration and the redirect_uri in authorize requests; sent again at token exchange.
rows.provider: redirect_uri "must match one of the redirect URIs you specified when registering your integration"; token-call redirect_uri must match the authorize one.

rows.claim: Scope needed for the GET /v2/users test call
rows.ours: Test uses GET /v2/users but lists only api:calls:read:basic / api:calls:create; api:users:read not named.
rows.provider: "When accessed through a Bearer token authorization method, this endpoint requires the scope 'api:users:read'." (Round 1 quote; the API docs page is JS-rendered and could not be re-read this round.)

rows.claim: Token exchange endpoint and client auth
rows.ours: POST app.gong.io/oauth2/generate-customer-token with HTTP Basic client_id:client_secret; grant_type=authorization_code body.
rows.provider: POST https://app.gong.io/oauth2/generate-customer-token, with HTTP Basic Base64(client_id:client_secret); grant_type=authorization_code, refresh via grant_type=refresh_token.

rows.ours: Code valid 10 minutes; access token 1 day by default; refresh token returned; refresh-token lifetime left open.
rows.provider: Access token "by default is valid for 1 day" (validity_duration overrides); refresh via grant_type=refresh_token; auth code valid 10 minutes. Refresh-token lifetime not stated.

rows.claim: Per-customer API base URL returned with the token
rows.composio: Enter https://api.gong.io as the base URL for most tenants.
rows.ours: Token returns api_base_url_for_customer; call the API at that URL.
rows.provider: "The api_base_url_for_customer is different for each customer and should be saved as part of the customer's context."

rows.claim: Public availability goes through the Gong Collective
rows.ours: Apps stay Private until Gong reviews and publishes them to the Gong Collective for customers to install.
rows.provider: "Publish the app in the Gong Collective. Your customers can then install the app on their instance of Gong." Apps are Private while being built.

rows.ours: Add trusted IPs, submit the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form; Gong contacts within five business days; total time unstated.
rows.provider: Trusted IPs required before publishing; submit the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form; Gong's team responds within five business days to finalize release and listing. No total review time or criteria published.

"By default Gong limits your company's access to the service to 3 API calls per second, and 10,000 API calls per day." (Round 1 quote; the API docs page is JS-rendered and could not be re-read this round.)
